title: Why Razor Refills Are Locked Up Like Jewelry
topic: Why Razor Refills Are Locked Up Like Jewelry
mechanism: Razor makers sell the handle cheap and make their money on refills that cost under thirty cents to make but sell for five dollars, so stores guard them like jewellery.

beats.hook: Macro: a $10 razor pack swings on its peg toward the lens; you grab it grinning; the $10 tag stamps on; you cheer WHAT A BARGAIN.
beats.story: Bathroom: the first shave is dolphin-smooth, you feel like a movie star.
beats.rise: Two weeks on, the blade tugs (you jump with an OUCH); you stroll to the store sure refills are a quick grab.
beats.twist: The refills sit in a LOCKED glass case between perfume, phones and watches; the clerk arrives with a giant key and rings up $40; you faint.
beats.mechanism: Cold lab: STEEL bin (<5¢), PLASTIC jar (3-5¢), balance with UNDER 30¢ vs a $5 tag that slams it down, a x15-20 dial; 1904 patent office stamp; factory belt HANDLE: ONCE / BLADES: FOREVER; neon stage blade race 2 → 7 blades and a razor-lawnmower.
beats.ending: Vault: a refill under a glass dome beside diamonds; back in the aisle a new guy grabs the $10 razor, loops into the hook.

seed.what: The LOCKED refill case behind the peg wall
